key_insight: Adding patient-reported outcomes to surrogate endpoints improved machine learning prediction of overall survival benefit in oncology trials.
clinical_relevance: Combining patient experience with efficacy endpoints could help assess treatment benefit in oncology drug development, without replacing overall survival follow-up.
method: Reviewed FDA approval-supporting oncology trials from 2013–2023 reporting overall survival, surrogate endpoints, and patient-reported outcomes.
Compared machine learning models using surrogate endpoints alone versus surrogate endpoints plus patient-reported outcomes.
Evaluated performance with repeated five-fold trial-grouped cross-validation and leave-one-trial-out validation.
evidence_signal: Across 100 trials involving 68,987 participants, adding patient-reported outcomes increased AUC-ROC from 0.67 to 0.79; leave-one-trial-out validation supported the improvement (difference 0.132; 95% CI, 0.017–0.248).
watch_item: Validation was internal to selected approval-supporting trials; generalizability to other trials and individual patient survival prediction remains unestablished.
paper_title: Improving Survival Prediction from Surrogate Endpoints Through Integration of Patient-Reported Outcomes Using Machine Learning
